content.text: {"headline":"Approve P1: borrow breaks, move 3 agents to payments, and add IVR callback and outage message, at no extra cost (₹9,351, same as doing nothing)","why":"The payments spike comes from the P1 UPI switch incident (INC-20261006-6998). At 10:30, 213 calls arrived against 111.9 forecast, service level fell to 4.7% and 59 calls were abandoned. Staffing and handle time are not the problem. P1 is predicted to reach 92.3% overall (payments 93.7%, general 90.5%) with 1.9% abandons. That is above the 80% target, follows policy and costs ₹9,351, the same as taking no action. Doing nothing is also forecast to recover (90.2%), so P1 is a free buffer in case UPI calls keep running high.","trade_offs":["P0 (no action) costs the same ₹9,351 and is forecast at 90.2%, but has less margin if the outage drags on, with 2.2% abandons vs 1.9%.","P2 targets the outage more directly with outage messaging on more call types and chat deflection. It reaches 94.0% with 1.2% abandons for ₹552 more (₹9,903).","P3 and P4 add overtime and reach 94.7% and 97.2% for ₹15,471 and ₹17,823. They cost ₹6,120–8,472 more for gains well above target.","General queue risk is low. Moving 3 agents still leaves general at 90.5%, which is predicted to be higher than with no action (89.8%)."],"watch":"Track the UPI incident status and upi_payment_failed volumes (recently 2.56x normal). If arrivals stay near the 10:30 level, or payments service level falls below 80% despite P1, move to P2 or add overtime. No escalation to the duty manager is needed now."}
